title: Two independent studies push semiconductor qubits towards practical scales
excerpt: Semiconductor spin qubits are one of the most promising building blocks for future quantum computers, but turning them into a working, large-scale quantum computer has so far proven difficult. content_html:
Semiconductor spin qubits are one of the most promising building blocks for future quantum computers, but turning them into a working, large-scale quantum computer has so far proven difficult. For now, two big questions remain open: how to connect qubits that aren't sitting right next to each other, and how to control huge numbers of them without an unmanageable tangle of wiring.

Now, two independent studies published in Nature have each reported new experiments tackling these problems head-on.

Roadblocks to scalability

A semiconductor qubit stores information in the quantum spin of a single electron, trapped inside a tiny silicon structure called a quantum dot. These electrons can be nudged into precise spin states using electrical signals, and pairs of neighboring electrons can be made to interact so that quantum operations can be performed on them.

Unlike some other qubit designs, semiconductor qubits can be made from materials and manufacturing techniques already used to build ordinary silicon chips. In principle, this should allow them to hold onto their fragile quantum information for comparatively long periods, making them naturally resistant to the noise and disturbance of the outside world.

However, these interactions normally only work over extremely short distances, meaning qubits usually need to be packed tightly together. That density leaves little room for the wiring and control hardware needed to operate each qubit individually, creating a serious obstacle to scaling the technology up.

Independent approaches

In one study, Lieven Vandersypen and colleagues at Delft University of Technology addressed this challenge by building a device that physically shuttles a single qubit back and forth over about 1.2 micrometers, so that it could interact with four other qubits stationed nearby. This mobility enabled the team to perform the kind of multi-qubit "parity checks" that underpin quantum error correction and use them to link five qubits together in a shared quantum state.

In the other study, members of the HRL Quantum Team instead focused on control: building a chip containing 54 quantum dots, each capable of hosting up to 18 qubits. These quantum dots were wired to a custom control chip, cooled just above the qubits' own operating temperature. To carry signals between the controller and the qubit chip, the team also connected them with a superconducting ribbon cable.

Connectivity and control

To verify their approach, the Delft group demonstrated genuine multi-qubit entanglement across all five qubits in their array. The HRL group used their system to run error-detection and error-correction routines, improving on previous qubit performance by roughly a factor of 10.

Together, the results tackle two separate bottlenecks of connectivity and control that any large-scale silicon quantum computer will eventually need to solve. Although there is some way to go before either approach can be implemented in a full-scale quantum computer, both teams' results could guide the future development of modular, replicable and scalable designs, perhaps paving the way for practical, silicon-based quantum computing.

content_html_zh:
半导体自旋量子位是未来量子计算机最有前途的构建模块之一，但迄今为止将其转变为可用的大型量子计算机已被证明是困难的。 目前，有两个大问题仍然悬而未决：如何连接彼此不相邻的量子位，以及如何控制大量量子位，而不需要难以管理的接线混乱。

现在，《自然》杂志上发表的两项独立研究都报告了正面解决这些问题的新实验。

可扩展性的障碍

半导体量子位将信息存储在单个电子的量子自旋中，该电子被困在称为量子点的微小硅结构内。 可以使用电信号将这些电子推入精确的自旋态，并且可以使相邻电子对相互作用，以便可以对它们执行量子操作。

与其他一些量子位设计不同，半导体量子位可以由已用于构建普通硅芯片的材料和制造技术制成。 原则上，这应该允许它们在相对较长的时间内保留脆弱的量子信息，使它们自然地抵抗外界的噪音和干扰。

然而，这些相互作用通常只能在极短的距离内起作用，这意味着量子位通常需要紧密地包装在一起。 这种密度为单独操作每个量子位所需的布线和控制硬件留下的空间很小，从而为扩大技术规模造成了严重障碍。

独立方法

在一项研究中，代尔夫特理工大学的 Lieven Vandersypen 及其同事通过构建一种设备来解决这一挑战，该设备可以在大约 1.2 微米的距离上物理地来回传输单个量子位，以便它可以与附近的其他四个量子位相互作用。 这种移动性使团队能够执行支持量子纠错的多量子位“奇偶校验”，并使用它们将五个量子位以共享量子状态连接在一起。

在另一项研究中，HRL 量子团队的成员转而专注于控制：构建一个包含 54 个量子点的芯片，每个量子点最多可容纳 18 个量子位。 这些量子点连接到定制的控制芯片，冷却温度略高于量子位自身的工作温度。 为了在控制器和量子位芯片之间传输信号，该团队还使用超导带状电缆将它们连接起来。

连接性和控制

为了验证他们的方法，代尔夫特研究小组在其阵列中的所有五个量子位上展示了真正的多量子位纠缠。 HRL 小组使用他们的系统运行错误检测和纠错例程，将之前的量子位性能提高了大约 10 倍。

这些结果共同解决了任何大型硅量子计算机最终都需要解决的两个独立的连接和控制瓶颈。 尽管这两种方法在全尺寸量子计算机中实现还有很长的路要走，但这两个团队的结果可以指导模块化、可复制和可扩展设计的未来发展，或许为实用的硅基量子计算铺平道路。
